text:
Predicates:
Twins(x) ::: x is a twin.
Triplets(x) ::: x is a triplet.
SpendTimeWith(x, y) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with y.
SameAge(x, y) ::: x and y are the same age.
Complain(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHome(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopBonds(x, y) ::: x develops strong bonds with y.
Person(x) ::: x is a person.

Premises:
∀x (Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x) → SpendTimeWith(x, x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x (SameAge(x, y) → Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x)) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (Complain(x) → SameAge(x, y)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHome(x) → ¬DevelopBonds(x, y)) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with their family members.
∀x (SpendTimeWith(x, y) → ¬LiveAtHome(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
(Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke)) ∧ DevelopBonds(luke, family) ⊕ ¬((Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke)) ∨ DevelopBonds(luke, family)) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family members, or he neither is a twin or triplet nor develops strong bonds with his family members.

Conclusion:
Complain(luke) ::: Luke complains often about annoying siblings.
